questions.q: What is the key difference between text-to-speech (TTS) and native speech-to-speech?
options: They are two names for the exact same capability
TTS only works in English, while speech-to-speech works in any language
Native speech-to-speech always requires a human in the loop
TTS converts text into audio; native speech-to-speech goes audio in, audio out, without a required text transcript step
questions.explain: TTS still starts from text. Native speech-to-speech skips the required text intermediate step entirely, which is what makes real-time voice agents possible.

questions.q: Which three realtime audio models does OpenAI currently offer, per its own documentation?
options: DALL-E, Whisper Classic, and ChatGPT Voice
GPT-Realtime-Whisper, GPT-Realtime-2, and GPT-Realtime-Translate
Sunburst, Flare, and Aurora
Just one single model that handles all audio tasks
questions.explain: OpenAI offers three distinct realtime models: Realtime-Whisper (streaming STT), Realtime-2 (a full voice agent), and Realtime-Translate (live speech-to-speech translation).

questions.q: What provider notably does NOT appear on this lesson's list of audio/speech-model providers, and why?
options: Google, because it has no audio products at all
OpenAI, because it only does text
Anthropic — Claude's voice mode is a product feature built from speech recognition plus a third-party TTS layer, not a general-purpose audio API
ElevenLabs, because it is not a real company
questions.explain: Anthropic doesn't expose a general audio content type in the Messages API; Claude's own voice mode wraps speech recognition and ElevenLabs' TTS around the text model.

questions.q: How does audio support compare to image support across Claude, GPT, and Gemini?
options: Image has three-way parity (all three accept an image content block); audio does not have that same parity yet
All three offer identical, unified audio and image support
None of the three providers support images
Audio has parity but image does not
questions.explain: Claude, GPT, and Gemini all accept an image content block in the same request shape. Audio doesn't have that same unified, three-way support yet.

questions.q: In a realistic Claude-based voice assistant architecture, how many separate API calls/models are typically chained together, and why?
options: Just one — Claude handles audio input and output directly
Two — Claude plus one TTS model
Three — an STT model to transcribe, Claude to reason over the text, and a separate TTS model to speak the reply
Zero — voice assistants don't use APIs
questions.explain: Because Claude has no native audio API, the realistic chain is: STT transcribes speech to text, Claude reasons over that text, and a separate TTS model speaks the reply back — three calls across two or three providers.
